evidence.explanation: oauthAuthorizeHandler reads client_id and scope but never reads/stores/validates a redirect_uri. Unconditionally 302s to internal /consent with no redirect_uri check. No registered redirect_uri lookup or exact-match comparison anywhere.
No state parameter is read, stored, or echoed at any step. CSRF protection via state is entirely absent.
Authorize handler appends only code to the /consent redirect. No iss parameter; no iss validation in consent/token handlers. Mix-up protection absent.
No code_challenge/code_challenge_method read or stored; token handler reads no code_verifier. PKCE not implemented at any step.
No PKCE; neither S256 nor plain handled. plain not explicitly rejected because no PKCE processing exists.
response_type is never inspected; response_type=token is not rejected.
grant_type is never inspected; grant_type=password is not rejected.
RetrieveAuthRequest calls authRequests.Load but never Delete. After a successful exchange the code persists in the sync.Map indefinitely — unlimited code replay.
No client authentication: no Basic Auth, no client_secret, no client registry lookup, no middleware on /oauth/token.
scopeFromForm read from POST body (line 216); authRequest.Scope available after line 220 but never compared. Token response (line 241) emits scopeFromForm directly — scope escalation to admin.
Only access_token/scope/token_type issued; no refresh token path.
PKCE absent for all client types.
Access token is a plain concatenated bearer string; no DPoP/mTLS proof-of-possession.
No resource parameter read; issued token carries no audience/resource constraint.
GenerateAuthCode() uses math/rand seeded with time.Now().UnixNano(), not crypto/rand. Authorization codes are predictable.
Token value is deterministic: "token_" + code + "_" + userID. Not cryptographically opaque.
Reflected XSS: c.Query("code") interpolated into an HTML attribute without escaping.

taint_pairs.rationale: scope tampering / privilege escalation — attacker-controlled scope flows to token response; authRequest.Scope never compared.
authorization code replay — no Delete follows a successful Load.
reflected XSS on consent page — code interpolated without html.EscapeString.
